newsitem.title: PERU: Peru president's rating lowest in 5 yrs - poll.
newsitem.headline: Peru president's rating lowest in 5 yrs - poll.

text.p: The public approval rating of President Alberto Fujimori dropped to its lowest level in five years to stand at 45 percent at the beginning of December, down from 52 percent a month earlier, according to leading Peruvian pollster Apoyo.
"It is the first time this has happened since 1991," said Apoyo director Alfredo Torres, on announcing the results of a survey of 400 Lima residents carried out on December 5 and 6.

The president's approval rating would have been even lower had he not proposed an amnesty for retired Gen. Rodolfo Robles, who was detained by the military for "insubordination" after alleging human rights abuses by the army, Torres said.
The Apoyo survey showed 75 percent of the population agreed with the amnesty for the general, who is regarded in Peru as a champion of human rights.
Fujimori's rating has steadily fallen through 1996 after he began the year with 75 percent of the population approving his performance as president, according to Apoyo.
Fujimori, who came to power in 1990 and was reelected with an overwhelming 64 percent of the vote last year, is considering running for a third consecutive term.
But the Apoyo poll showed 51 percent would vote against allowing him to run again if a referendum were held on the issue.
Fujimori has had relatively high popularity ratings during his term due mainly to the virtual defeat of communist guerrillas, economic reform and strong, personalized leadership style.

But the administration's failure to reduce high levels of poverty and unemployment, Fujimori's perceived authoritarianism, his possible bid for a third term, and the influence of his shadowy security adviser Vladimiro Montesinos, are starting to take a toll on the president's popularity, analysts say.
